question: The 10-year-old Italian child Adelio Bocci, the son of an Italian father and a Tajik mother who is a naturalised Italian, is currently in Kazakhstan. According to local press reports, the mother removed him from the family home and took him to Kazakhstan.

Three international arrest warrants and one extradition request have been issued for the mother, continue the reports, while Italian diplomatic staff and Interpol have been unable to offer clear information as to the child’s safety.

The not-for-profit association for families and missing persons ‘Penelope’ recently wrote to the Italian Foreign Minister pointing to photos and videos in which the child shows signs of having been beaten, and in which he seems fearful and submissive.

How does the Vice-President of the Commission/High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy intend to support the efforts of Italian diplomatic staff to facilitate and ensure the safety of Adelio Bocci and his mother, not least in view of the 2015 Enhanced Partnership and Cooperation Agreement (EPCA), which brought relations to Kazakhstan to a new level and represents an important milestone in EU relations with Kazakhstan dating back over 25 years now?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.3.2024) The EU is aware about the case of Adelio Bocci and is in close contact with the Italian embassy in Kazakhstan regarding his situation. In the best interest of the child, it is important to ensure that the father is guaranteed the possibility of meeting his child, via video call and also in person, if he decides to travel to Kazakhstan.

The EU and Kazakhstan have an annual extensive dialogue on Justice and Home Affairs matters, including on the proper implementation of the relevant international conventions. The EU will continue to monitor the situation closely, including in cooperation with the Italian embassy.
